correctness.rationale: The Hilbert–Schmidt kernel 1_{s<t} on L²(dt+aδ_{1/2}) has trace norm-square 1/2+a, excluding the atom self-pair. The range is an energy space with u(0)=0, atomic value u_-(1/2), independent one-sided traces and jump stiffness [u]²/a; norm includes a|u_-(1/2)|². The variational problem E(u,v)=κ²N(u,v) has Dirichlet/Neumann endpoints and two interface laws, whose determinant factors into cos(κ/2)-(aκ±1)sin(κ/2). Because cot(κ/2)-aκ is strictly decreasing on every (2πm,2π(m+1)), each branch has exactly one simple root, in strict order; no pole roots are missed. Expanding κ=2πm+2/(a2πm)±2/(a²(2πm)²)+... gives m⁴(s_{2m+1}-s_{2m+2})→1/(4π⁴a²), s_n~1/(πn), and S_p iff p>1. Independently checked algebraic determinant factorization and high-m roots for a=0.7,2 at m=40,150,600; for a=2, m=600 gives 0.000641623665 vs predicted 0.000641623891. Finite roots are diagnostic, not infinite proof.
residual_risks: The result uses strict [0,t) integration, an atom exactly at midpoint, and fixed a>0; changing these conventions changes interface conditions.
